Guides

Coming from Express

Map an Express app onto routiva: what stays identical, what changes, and where Express still wins.

The mental model is unchanged#

An app is a router. A router is an ordered list of layers. A layer is a route, a piece of middleware, or an error handler. next() moves a request down the list, and registration order is execution order. None of that changes when you move from Express to routiva.

The handler signatures are identical, so most route bodies copy over untouched. A function (req, res, next) is middleware in both. A four-arity function (err, req, res, next) is an error handler in both.

API mapping#

Expressroutiva
const app = express()const app = createApp() or new App()
app.use(fn)app.use(fn)
app.use('/api', router)app.use('/api', router)
app.get/post/put/patch/delete/head/optionsidentical, plus app.all()
express.Router()new Router()
express.json()json() or App.json()
express.urlencoded({ extended: true })urlencoded({ extended: true })
express.static('public')serveStatic('public')
express.text() / express.raw()text() / raw()
req.params, req.query, req.body, req.cookiesidentical
req.get(name) / req.header(name)identical
res.status/json/send/redirect/type/set/cookieidentical
res.sendFile(path) / res.download(path)identical
req.accepts() / res.format()identical
next(err)identical
app.use((err, req, res, next) => {})identical
app.listen(port, cb)identical; returns the http.Server

The cors, compression, express-rate-limit, morgan, cookie-parser and serve-static imports disappear. Their equivalents are exported by routiva and used the same way.

Same shape, less ceremony#

A users endpoint in Express, with the packages it needs:

js
import express from 'express';
import cors from 'cors';
import compression from 'compression';

const app = express();
app.use(cors());
app.use(compression());
app.use(express.json());

app.get('/users/:id', async (req, res, next) => {
  try {
    const user = await db.find(req.params.id);
    if (!user) return res.status(404).json({ error: 'not found' });
    res.json(user);
  } catch (err) {
    next(err);          // Express 4 needs this
  }
});

app.listen(3000);

The routiva version:

js
import { createApp, cors, compress, json } from 'routiva';

const app = createApp();
app.use(cors());
app.use(compress());
app.use(json());

app.get('/users/:id', async (req, res) => {
  const user = await db.find(req.params.id);   // a rejection is forwarded
  if (!user) return res.status(404).json({ error: 'not found' });
  res.json(user);
});

app.listen(3000);

The route body does not change. The try/catch, the extra imports and the separate packages do.

What differs#

Async errors are handled for you#

Express 4 only forwards synchronous throws to error middleware. A rejected promise inside an async handler hangs the request unless you wrap it. routiva attaches .catch(next) to the value every handler returns, so throw and Promise.reject both reach your error middleware. Express 5 catches async errors too; routiva matches that behaviour.

405 with an Allow header#

If a path matches but the method does not, routiva answers 405 Method Not Allowed with a correct Allow header. Express returns 404. For a path that exists, routiva answers OPTIONS automatically with 204 and the same Allow list, and HEAD reuses the matching GET route with the body suppressed.

One response, once#

res.send() and res.json() are guarded by res.raw.headersSent and res.raw.writableEnded. A stray second res.json() is a no-op instead of an ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT crash.

Body parse errors have stable types#

json() rejects a body that is not an object or array with 400 entity.parse.failed, and an oversized body with 413 entity.too.large. The type value is set on the error, so one error handler can map both.

No template engine or view system#

There is no res.render(), no app.set('view engine', ...), no views directory, no view cache and no app.locals. If your app renders HTML on the server, keep Express or render it yourself and call res.send(). One minor detail: res.locals exists as an empty object on each response, but nothing in the framework reads it for you.

Smaller path syntax#

routiva supports :name parameters and a * wildcard. Express also supports optional parameters (:id?), inline regex (:id(\d+)) and arrays of paths. Port those by validating inside router.param() or the handler.

Where Express still wins#

  • Ecosystem. Thousands of mature middlewares, adapters and integrations.
  • Rendering. Any template engine via res.render().
  • Sessions, flash, auth. Passport and its strategies are Express-shaped.
  • Advanced routing. Optional params, regex params and path arrays.
  • Streaming compression. routiva compresses buffered res.send() output; streamed files pass through untouched. Express's compression wraps the whole response stream.
  • Track record. Express has years of production hardening. routiva is a compact, well-tested implementation.

Use Express when the ecosystem is doing real work for you. Use routiva when you want the same mental model inside a core you can read end to end.

A migration checklist#

  1. Replace express() with createApp() and swap require for an import.
  2. Move CORS, compression and rate limiting to routiva's bundled factories.
  3. Drop cookie-parser; req.cookies is already parsed.
  4. Replace express.json() with json({ limit: '100kb' }).
  5. Delete the try/catch plus next(err) wrappers around async handlers.
  6. Replace res.render() call sites before you start.
  7. Run your suite against the new app. Most handler bodies will not have changed.
